title: False sharing — cache line invalidation, padding, @Contended

s1_definition.profdef: **False sharing** occurs when two threads write to DIFFERENT variables that happen to reside on the SAME CPU cache line (typically 64 bytes). When Thread-1 writes variable-A, the CPU invalidates the ENTIRE cache line on Thread-2's core — even though Thread-2 only uses variable-B (which is on the same line but wasn't modified). Thread-2 must reload the line from main memory. This causes constant cache invalidation ping-pong between cores — performance drops 10-100x for what LOOKS like independent, non-shared data. **Fix**: pad variables so each is on its OWN cache line (64 bytes apart). Java 8+: `@jdk.internal.vm.annotation.Contended` (or `@sun.misc.Contended`) auto-pads. `LongAdder` uses `@Contended` internally for its cells.
s1_definition.analogy: Two tellers at separate desks, each with their OWN calculator. But the calculators are on the SAME shared desk shelf. When Teller-1 presses a button on their calculator, the ENTIRE shelf shakes → Teller-2's calculator display resets! Teller-2 must re-read their number. They're not SHARING data — but they're sharing the SHELF (cache line). Fix: put each calculator on its OWN separate shelf (padding). No more shaking!
s1_definition.oneliner: False sharing = different variables, same cache line (64 bytes). One thread writes → entire line invalidated on other cores → 10-100x slowdown. Fix: @Contended padding (64-byte separation). LongAdder uses this internally.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** **False sharing** occurs when two threads write to DIFFERENT variables that happen to reside on the SAME CPU cache line (typically 64 bytes). **In simple words (banking analogy):** Two tellers at separate desks, each with their OWN calculator. But the calculators are on the SAME shared desk shelf. sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The high-frequency trading (HFT) counter had two AtomicLongs:** `buyCount` and `sellCount`, incremented by separate threads (buy thread + sell thread). Both AtomicLongs allocated adjacently → same cache line. Performance: 50M ops/sec (expected 500M on 2 cores). 10x slower due to false sharing! Fix: padded each counter to its own cache line. Performance: 480M ops/sec. Or: used two separate `LongAdder` instances (internally @Contended padded).
sections.s4e_build:
```bash
mvn clean test
# FalseSharingTest: 2 tests — all pass!
# Output: "False sharing: ~300ms, Padded: ~80ms, Speedup: 3-5x"
```
sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** `counter1` and `counter2` are 8 bytes each, allocated adjacently → both on the same 64-byte cache line.

**Step 2 (false sharing).** Core-1 writes `counter1` → cache line INVALIDATED on Core-2 (MESI protocol). Core-2 writes `counter2` → cache line INVALIDATED on Core-1. Constant ping-pong: ~100ns per write instead of ~5ns.

**Step 3 (padded).** 56 bytes padding between counters → each on its OWN cache line. Core-1 writes counter1 → Core-2's cache line NOT invalidated (different line!). Each write: ~5ns. 10-20x faster!
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ FALSE SHARING ═══

  Cache line (64 bytes): [counter1 | counter2 | padding...]
  Core-1 writes counter1 → INVALIDATES entire line on Core-2!
  Core-2 writes counter2 → INVALIDATES entire line on Core-1!
  Ping-pong: 100ns per op! 10x slower!

  ═══ PADDED (no false sharing) ═══

  Cache line 1: [counter1 | padding (56 bytes)]
  Cache line 2: [counter2 | padding (56 bytes)]
  Core-1 writes counter1 → Core-2's line NOT affected!
  No ping-pong: 5ns per op! 10x faster!
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — CPU Cache Architecture ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  CPU Core-1                           │
  │  L1 Cache:                           │
  │  Line[42]: [counter1|counter2|...]   │  ← SHARED line!
  │  Write counter1 → line DIRTY         │
  │  → MESI: invalidate line on Core-2!  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  CPU Core-2                           │
  │  L1 Cache:                           │
  │  Line[42]: INVALID! Must reload!     │
  │  Read counter2 → fetch from L3/RAM!  │ ~100ns!
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ═══ @Contended FIX ═══

  @Contended class Cell {
      volatile long value;
  }
  // JVM adds 128 bytes padding before + after!
  // Each Cell on its own cache line! Zero invalidation!

  LongAdder internally:
  Cell[] cells; // each Cell is @Contended → own cache line!
  Thread-1 → cells[0].value++ (Core-1 cache line A)
  Thread-2 → cells[1].value++ (Core-2 cache line B)
  No invalidation! Maximum throughput!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
False sharing: two threads write to INDEPENDENT variables that share the same CPU cache line (64 bytes). Each write invalidates the entire cache line on other cores — constant cache invalidation ping-pong. Performance drops 10-100x for what looks like completely independent data. Fix: pad variables to separate cache lines — manual padding (56 bytes of longs between fields) or `@Contended` annotation (JVM adds 128 bytes automatically).

`LongAdder` is fast BECAUSE of this: its internal `Cell` class uses `@Contended` — each thread's cell is on its own cache line, zero false sharing. That's why LongAdder is 10x faster than AtomicLong under high contention. In HFT banking: buy counter + sell counter on adjacent memory → 50M ops/sec. After padding: 480M ops/sec. False sharing is invisible in profilers (no lock contention shown) — only visible via hardware cache miss counters (perf stat, JMH @AuxCounters).

---
